label: copy-phase input digit 3 (fed-back 3, not the first original token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is the digit 3 (the model fed back its previous output 3). Never fires on original-phase or delimiter steps, on any other token, or when 3 was the first original token (recall_idx 1). Recall is 100%. About 24% of predicted steps stay silent, and these misses have no clean pattern. The strongest activations come from a 3 at original position 2-3 near the start of the copy. A second consecutive 3 is weaker, and a 3 very late in the copy is often weak or absent.

issues: The core claims check out. On dev, all 57146 activations are in the copy phase, all have in_tok == 3, and none are at recall_idx 0/1. Test recall is 1.0, with 0 missed activations and mass recall 1.0.

The explanation says the 24% of silent predicted steps have no clean pattern. That is not accurate: the silences are structured. Precision of (copy & in_tok==3) on dev: recall_idx 2 (3 at original position 1) = 0.52; to_go==0 (3 fed back at the final step) = 0.69; r=2 & to_go=0 = 0.23. Mid-copy cells reach 0.92-0.97 (e.g. r=3 to_go=2-4, r=4 to_go=2-4). At recall_idx 2 the feature is also more often silent when 3 is repeated in the original (in_count>=2: precision 0.37, vs 0.55 for in_count==1).

The claim that a second consecutive 3 is weaker is not visible as a firing-rate difference: with prev_tok==3, precision is 0.74 vs 0.76 otherwise. It may still hold for magnitude, and the top examples do show the second 3 at about 0.3-0.6 of max.

These are graded effects (weaker activation that drops below threshold), not a separable class. Boolean refinements barely improve test F1 (0.863 -> 0.868), and the strict recall_idx>=3 & to_go>=1 drops to 0.746. So the simple predicate and label stand. The explanation should say that silence concentrates at recall_idx 2 and at the final step.
